Shared clause-parsing helper for case_match()/recode_values()

Source: R/ir.R
ir_parse_value_match_clauses.Rd

Both functions share an identical clause shape once "match by value" is expressed as %in%: f(x, old_values_1 ~ new_value_1, ..., <default_key> = value). Builds x %in% old_values_i as each clause's condition (reusing the existing %in% op verbatim, including its NA-matching semantics) and hands the interleaved cond/value list to ir_call( "case_when", ...) directly – case_match()/recode_values() are, at the IR level, indistinguishable from case_when() once desugared this way.

Usage

ir_parse_value_match_clauses(expr, env, schema, default_key)

Arguments

expr

The raw case_match(...)/recode_values(...) call

env

The quosure's environment

schema

List with names/types

default_key

".default" (case_match) or "default" (recode_values) – the one named control argument supported

Value

An ir_call("case_when", ...) node, or NULL if unsupported

Details

Only the two-sided-formula clause interface is supported: recode_values()'s from=/to=/unmatched=/ptype= vector-lookup-table interface, and case_match()'s .ptype=, are NOT supported – ANY named argument other than default_key present in the call makes this return NULL (caller falls back).

A clause's LHS ("old value(s)") must resolve to a literal (a constant, a c(...) vector, or an environment lookup) – an LHS referencing a column is unsupported (mirrors %in%'s own RHS restriction, since that's exactly the op this desugars into). A STRING-vs-non-STRING type mismatch between x and a clause's LHS is diagnosed here (mirroring na_if()'s own STRING compatibility check) rather than surfacing as a raw cudf cast error at lowering time.
